gst-registration.meta: GST Registration online in India made simple. Know who needs it, documents required, fees, process and timeline. Expert help from Tax Alphonic.
gst-registration.intro: If you run a business in India and your sales cross a certain limit, the law says you must register for GST. It sounds complicated, but it really is not. GST registration simply gives your business a special number (called a GSTIN) that lets you collect tax from customers and claim back the tax you pay on your purchases. Think of it as your business's tax identity card.
gst-registration.whatIs: GST stands for Goods and Services Tax. It is one single tax that replaced many older taxes like VAT, service tax and excise duty. When you register, the government gives you a 15-digit GSTIN number. This number goes on all your bills. Without it, you cannot legally charge GST, and big companies often will not work with you because they cannot claim their input credit.
benefits: You can legally collect tax and issue proper tax invoices
You can claim back the GST you pay on your own purchases (called input tax credit), which saves real money
Bigger clients and companies prefer working with GST-registered businesses
You can sell across all states of India without trouble
It makes your business look trustworthy and professional
It is needed to sell on Amazon, Flipkart and other online platforms
who: Businesses with yearly sales above Rs 40 lakh (Rs 20 lakh for services, and Rs 10-20 lakh in some special states)
Anyone selling online on Amazon, Flipkart, etc.
Businesses selling goods from one state to another
People who want to claim input tax credit
Casual or seasonal businesses
docs: PAN card of the business or owner
Proof of business address (electricity bill, rent agreement, etc.)
Bank account details (cancelled cheque or statement)
process: We collect your documents and basic business details
We fill and submit your GST application on the government portal
We handle the Aadhaar verification step for you
The GST officer reviews the application
Your GSTIN number is issued, usually within 3 to 7 working days
We hand over your GST certificate and explain your next steps
faqs: How long does GST registration take?
Usually 3 to 7 working days once all your documents are ready. Sometimes the officer may ask a question, which can add a couple of days.
Is GST registration free?
The government does not charge a fee for registration. You only pay a professional fee for expert help to make sure it is done correctly the first time.
Do I need GST if my sales are small?
If your sales are below the limit (Rs 40 lakh for goods, Rs 20 lakh for services), it is optional. But many small businesses still register to claim input credit and look professional.
What happens if I don't register but should have?
You can face penalties and interest on the tax you should have collected. It is much cheaper to register on time.
Can I register from home?
Yes, the whole process is online. You do not need to visit any office.

trademark-registration.meta: Trademark Registration in India — protect your brand name and logo for 10 years. Simple guide on process, documents, fees and timeline by Tax Alphonic.
trademark-registration.intro: Your brand name and logo are how customers recognise you. Imagine spending years building a good name, and then someone else copies it. A trademark stops that. It gives you the legal right to your name and logo across all of India, so no one else can use them. It is one of the smartest, cheapest things you can do to protect your business.
trademark-registration.whatIs: A trademark is a legal protection for your brand identity — your business name, logo, tagline or even a unique sound or colour. Once registered, you get the right to put the ® symbol next to your brand, and you can take legal action against anyone who copies it. A trademark lasts 10 years and can be renewed forever.
benefits: No one else can legally use your brand name or logo in India
You can use the ® symbol, which builds customer trust
It becomes a valuable business asset you can sell or license
It protects you in court if someone copies your brand
It stops others from registering a similar name
Protection lasts 10 years and can be renewed forever
who: Any business owner who wants to protect their brand name
Startups building a new brand
Shops, restaurants and online sellers
Anyone with a unique logo, name or tagline
Businesses planning to grow or franchise
docs: Your brand name and logo (image file)
A signed form we prepare for you (Form TM-48)
List of goods or services your brand covers
process: We do a free search to check if your brand name is available
We pick the right class (category) for your business
We prepare and file your trademark application
You can start using the ™ symbol right away
The trademark office examines your application
If there are no objections, your mark is published and then registered
You get the ® symbol, usually within 12 to 18 months
faqs: Can I use my brand before registration is complete?
Yes. Once you file, you can use the ™ symbol immediately. The ® symbol comes after full registration.
How long does trademark registration take?
Filing is quick, but full registration takes about 12 to 18 months because of government processing. The good news is your protection starts from the filing date.
What if my name is already taken?
Our free search checks this first. If it is taken, we help you pick a strong, available name before filing.
Does one trademark cover all of India?
Yes, a registered trademark protects you across all of India.
What is a class in trademark?
Goods and services are divided into 45 classes. You register in the class that matches your business. We pick the right one for you.

private-limited-company-registration.meta: Register a Private Limited Company in India online. Simple guide on benefits, documents, process, fees and timeline. Expert help by Tax Alphonic.
private-limited-company-registration.intro: A Private Limited Company is the most popular way to start a serious business in India, especially if you plan to grow or raise money one day. It separates you from your business legally — so if the business owes money, your personal savings and home stay protected. It also makes investors and banks take you seriously.
private-limited-company-registration.whatIs: A Private Limited Company is a business that is registered with the government as its own legal 'person'. It can own property, take loans and sign contracts in its own name. It needs at least two directors and two shareholders (which can be the same people). The owners' personal money is protected — this is called limited liability.
benefits: Your personal assets (home, savings) are protected if the business has losses
Investors and venture capital firms prefer this structure
It is easier to raise loans and funding
The company continues even if owners change
It looks more credible to customers and partners
Ownership can be easily shared or transferred
who: Startups planning to raise investment
Founders with co-founders or partners
Businesses that want to grow big
Anyone who wants personal asset protection
Businesses that want a professional image
docs: Address proof (bank statement or utility bill)
Proof of office address (rent agreement or electricity bill)
A No Objection letter from the property owner
process: We get Digital Signatures (DSC) for all directors
We apply for Director Identification Numbers (DIN)
We reserve your company name with the government
We prepare and file all incorporation documents
The government reviews and approves
You receive your Certificate of Incorporation, PAN and TAN
Your company is officially born, usually in 7 to 10 working days
faqs: How many people do I need to start?
At least two — two directors and two shareholders. The same two people can play both roles.
How long does it take?
Usually 7 to 10 working days once all documents are ready.
Can I register a company at my home address?
Yes, you can use a residential address as your registered office with the proper proof.
What is limited liability?
It means your personal money and property are safe even if the company faces losses. You only risk what you invested in the company.
Do I need a minimum amount of money?
No, there is no minimum capital required by law. You can start small.

income-tax-filing.meta: Income Tax Return (ITR) filing online in India. Simple guide on who must file, documents needed, process and deadlines. Expert help by Tax Alphonic.
income-tax-filing.intro: Every year, if you earn above a certain amount, the government expects you to tell them how much you earned and how much tax you paid. This is called filing your Income Tax Return, or ITR. Many people find it scary, but it is really just a yearly report of your income. Filing on time keeps you on the right side of the law and can even get you a refund if you paid extra tax.
income-tax-filing.whatIs: An Income Tax Return (ITR) is a form where you declare your income, deductions and the tax you have paid for the year. Based on this, the government checks if you paid the right amount. If you paid too much, you get a refund. If you paid too little, you pay the difference. There are different ITR forms for salaried people, business owners and companies — we pick the right one for you.
benefits: You stay fully legal and avoid penalties
You can claim a refund if you paid extra tax
It acts as proof of income for loans and visas
It helps you carry forward business losses to save tax later
It builds a clean financial record
It is required for many tenders and government work
who: Salaried people earning above the basic exemption limit
Business owners and self-employed professionals
Anyone who wants to claim a tax refund
People applying for loans or visas (ITR is proof of income)
Companies and firms (filing is mandatory)
docs: Details of other income (rent, interest, etc.)
Investment proofs for deductions (LIC, PPF, etc.)
Details of any tax already paid (TDS)
process: We collect your income details and documents
We calculate your total income and tax correctly
We find every deduction you are eligible for, to save you tax
We pick the correct ITR form for your situation
We file your return on the income tax portal
We share the confirmation and help with any refund follow-up
faqs: Who must file an income tax return?
Anyone whose income is above the basic exemption limit must file. Even below it, filing is useful for refunds and as income proof.
What is the last date to file ITR?
For most individuals it is 31st July of the assessment year. Filing late can attract a penalty, so it is best to file early.
Will I get a refund?
If you paid more tax than required (often through TDS), yes — you get the extra back as a refund after filing.
What documents do I need?
Mainly your PAN, Aadhaar, Form 16 if salaried, bank statements, and proofs of any investments or deductions.
Can you file for business income too?
Yes, we handle ITR for salaried people, professionals, businesses and companies.

fssai-registration.meta: FSSAI Registration and food license online in India. Know who needs it, types, documents, fees and process. Fast expert help by Tax Alphonic.
fssai-registration.intro: If your business deals with food in any way — making it, packing it, selling it, or even running a small food stall — the law requires an FSSAI license. It is the government's way of making sure food sold to people is safe. Getting it also builds trust with your customers, because they can see your food business is officially approved.
fssai-registration.whatIs: FSSAI stands for Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. An FSSAI registration or license is permission from this authority to run a food business. There are three types depending on your size: Basic Registration (for small businesses), State License (for medium businesses), and Central License (for large businesses or those working across states). We help you figure out which one you need and get it.
benefits: You can legally run your food business
It builds customer trust — people prefer FSSAI-approved food
You can display the FSSAI number on your products and shop
It is needed to sell food on Swiggy, Zomato and online
It helps you avoid heavy fines for running without a license
It opens doors to bigger clients and tenders
who: Restaurants, cafes and cloud kitchens
Food stalls, sweet shops and bakeries
Food manufacturers and packers
Grocery stores and supermarkets
Online food sellers and home-based food businesses
Importers and exporters of food
docs: Details of the food products you deal with
For larger licenses: a food safety plan
process: We check your business size and tell you which license you need
We collect your documents and product details
We fill and submit your FSSAI application
The food authority reviews your application
For bigger licenses, an inspection may happen — we guide you through it
Your FSSAI registration or license is issued, usually in 7 to 15 working days
faqs: Do I really need FSSAI for a small food stall?
Yes. Even the smallest food business needs at least a Basic FSSAI Registration. It is the law and protects you from fines.
What are the three types of FSSAI license?
Basic Registration (small businesses under Rs 12 lakh turnover), State License (medium businesses), and Central License (large businesses or those operating in multiple states).
How long does it take?
Basic registration is faster (a few days). State and Central licenses take about 7 to 15 working days, sometimes more if an inspection is needed.
Can I sell on Swiggy or Zomato without FSSAI?
No. Online food platforms require a valid FSSAI license before they let you sell.
How long is the license valid?
You can choose a validity of 1 to 5 years. We remind you before it expires so you can renew on time.

proprietorship-registration.meta: Proprietorship Registration in India — the simplest way to start a business. Know benefits, documents, process and who it suits. Easy expert help by Tax Alphonic.
proprietorship-registration.intro: A proprietorship is the easiest and cheapest way to start a business in India. It is just you — one person — running your own business under your own name or a trade name. There is very little paperwork, no complex rules, and you can start almost immediately. For small shops, freelancers and home businesses, this is usually the best first step.
proprietorship-registration.whatIs: A sole proprietorship is a business owned and run by one single person. In the eyes of the law, you and your business are the same — there is no separate company. This makes it simple to start and run, but it also means you are personally responsible for everything the business does. There is no special registration certificate; instead, you register through things like GST, Shop Act or MSME to prove your business exists.
benefits: Easiest and cheapest business to start
Very little paperwork and compliance
You keep full control and all the profits
Quick to set up — start almost immediately
Low cost to run year after year
Ideal for testing a new business idea
who: Freelancers and consultants
Small shop owners and traders
Home-based businesses
People testing a new business idea
Anyone who wants the simplest possible setup
docs: Any one registration like GST, Shop Act or MSME
process: We understand your business and suggest the right registrations
We collect your documents
We apply for the registrations that prove your business exists (like GST, MSME or Shop Act)
We open your business in your trade name
You receive your registration proofs, usually within a few working days
We guide you on basic compliance going forward
faqs: Is a proprietorship registered like a company?
No. There is no single company certificate. You prove your business exists through registrations like GST, Shop Act or MSME, which we help you get.
What is the biggest risk of a proprietorship?
You are personally responsible for the business. If the business owes money, your personal savings can be used to pay it. For bigger or riskier businesses, an LLP or company is safer.
How fast can I start?
Very fast — often within a few working days, since there is minimal paperwork.
Can I convert it to a company later?
Yes. Many people start as a proprietor and later convert to an LLP or Private Limited Company as they grow. We help with that too.
Do I need GST for a proprietorship?
Only if your sales cross the GST limit or you sell online. Otherwise it is optional.

partnership-firm-registration.meta: Partnership Firm Registration in India — start a business with partners easily. Know benefits, documents, process and timeline. Expert help by Tax Alphonic.
partnership-firm-registration.intro: A partnership is when two or more people come together to run a business and share the profits. It is a simple way to start when you have a partner or two and want to keep things flexible. A written partnership deed sets out who does what and who gets what share — so everyone is clear from day one and there are no fights later.
partnership-firm-registration.whatIs: A partnership firm is a business owned by two or more partners who agree to share profits and responsibilities. The rules between partners are written in a document called a partnership deed. Registering the firm is optional but strongly recommended, because a registered firm has stronger legal rights — for example, it can sue others to recover money.
benefits: Easy and affordable to start
Shared work, shared responsibility, shared funds
Flexible — partners decide their own rules
A registered firm has stronger legal rights
Less compliance than a company
Good for family businesses and small partnerships
who: Two or more people starting a business together
Family-run businesses
Small and medium trading or service businesses
Professionals teaming up
Anyone wanting a simple shared-ownership structure
docs: PAN and Aadhaar of all partners
The partnership deed (we draft this for you)
process: We understand your business and the role of each partner
We draft a clear partnership deed covering profit share, duties and rules
All partners sign the deed
We register the firm with the Registrar of Firms (recommended)
We help you get PAN and other registrations for the firm
You receive your firm documents, usually within 7 to 12 working days
faqs: Is registering a partnership compulsory?
No, it is optional — but a registered firm has much stronger legal rights, like the ability to recover money through court. We always recommend registering.
What is a partnership deed?
It is a written agreement between partners that says who owns what share, who does what, and how profits and losses are split. We draft it carefully to avoid future disputes.
How is a partnership different from an LLP?
In a normal partnership, partners are personally responsible for the firm's debts. An LLP protects partners' personal money. If you want that protection, choose an LLP.
How many partners can there be?
A partnership can have between 2 and 20 partners.
Can we change the deed later?
Yes, partners can update the deed by mutual agreement. We help you make changes properly.

one-person-company-registration.meta: One Person Company (OPC) Registration in India — limited liability for solo founders. Benefits, documents, process and timeline explained. Expert help by Tax Alphonic.
one-person-company-registration.intro: A One Person Company, or OPC, is made for solo founders who want the protection of a company but do not have a partner. It gives you the best of both worlds — you run the business alone, but your personal money stays protected if the business has losses. It is a great choice if you are serious about your business and want it to look professional.
one-person-company-registration.whatIs: An OPC is a company owned by just one person. Unlike a proprietorship, an OPC is a separate legal entity — meaning the company is treated as its own 'person' in law. This gives you limited liability, so your personal savings are protected. You only need one director and one shareholder (the same person), plus one nominee who takes over if something happens to you.
benefits: Run a real company alone — no partner needed
Your personal money is protected (limited liability)
Looks more professional than a proprietorship
Easier to get loans and build credibility
The business continues through your nominee
Lower compliance than a Private Limited Company
who: Solo founders who want a company structure
Freelancers and consultants going professional
Single owners who want personal asset protection
People not ready to bring in partners yet
Anyone wanting a credible one-person business
docs: PAN and Aadhaar of the owner
Address proof (bank statement or utility bill)
Details of one nominee (with their consent)
A No Objection letter from the property owner
process: We get your Digital Signature (DSC)
We apply for your Director Identification Number (DIN)
We reserve your company name
We prepare and file incorporation documents, including the nominee details
The government reviews and approves
You receive your Certificate of Incorporation, PAN and TAN, usually in 7 to 10 working days
faqs: What is a nominee in an OPC?
A nominee is a person you name who will take over the company if you pass away or cannot run it. This keeps your business safe and continuous. The nominee must agree in writing.
How is OPC better than a proprietorship?
An OPC protects your personal money (limited liability) and is a proper company, which looks more professional. A proprietorship does not give this protection.
Can an OPC have more than one director?
An OPC has one shareholder, but it can have more than one director if needed. Only one person owns it.
Is there a turnover limit for OPC?
If your OPC grows beyond certain limits, it may need to convert to a Private Limited Company. We guide you when that time comes.
How long does it take?
Usually 7 to 10 working days once all documents are ready.

llp-registration.meta: LLP Registration in India — limited liability with simple compliance. Benefits, documents, process and timeline explained simply. Expert help by Tax Alphonic.
llp-registration.intro: An LLP, or Limited Liability Partnership, is a popular choice for professionals and small businesses with partners. It combines the flexibility of a partnership with the safety of a company. Your personal money is protected, the compliance is lighter than a company, and partners are not responsible for each other's mistakes. It is a smart, safe middle path.
llp-registration.whatIs: An LLP is a partnership where the partners have limited liability — meaning their personal assets are protected if the business has debts or losses. It is a separate legal entity, so the LLP itself can own property and sign contracts. Each partner is responsible only for their own actions, not for another partner's wrongdoing. It needs at least two partners and is run as per an LLP agreement.
benefits: Your personal assets are protected (limited liability)
Lighter compliance than a Private Limited Company
Partners are not liable for each other's mistakes
Flexible — partners set their own agreement
A separate legal entity that can own property
Great for professional firms and service businesses
who: Professional firms (CA, legal, consulting, design)
Small and medium businesses with partners
Service businesses that want liability protection
Startups not seeking equity investment
Anyone wanting partnership flexibility with company-like safety
docs: PAN and Aadhaar of all partners
A No Objection letter from the property owner
The LLP agreement (we draft this for you)
process: We get Digital Signatures (DSC) for partners
We apply for Designated Partner Identification Numbers (DPIN)
We reserve your LLP name
We file the incorporation documents
We draft and file your LLP agreement
You receive your Certificate of Incorporation, usually in 10 to 15 working days
faqs: How is an LLP different from a normal partnership?
In a normal partnership, partners are personally responsible for the firm's debts. In an LLP, your personal money is protected. That safety is the main reason people choose an LLP.
How is an LLP different from a Private Limited Company?
An LLP has lighter compliance and is great if you do not plan to raise equity investment. A Private Limited Company is better if you want to bring in investors.
How many partners do I need?
At least two. There is no upper limit on the number of partners.
What is an LLP agreement?
It is a document that sets out the rights, duties and profit share of each partner. We draft it carefully for you.
Is an LLP good for raising investment?
Investors usually prefer a Private Limited Company for equity funding. If raising investment is your main goal, we may suggest a Pvt Ltd instead.

section-8-company-registration.meta: Section 8 Company Registration in India — for NGOs and non-profits. Benefits, documents, process and tax exemptions explained simply by Tax Alphonic.
section-8-company-registration.intro: A Section 8 Company is the most respected way to run a non-profit or charitable organisation in India. If your goal is to help society — through education, charity, environment, art or social welfare — and not to earn profit for yourself, this structure gives you credibility and tax benefits. It is the NGO version of a company, with strong legal standing.
section-8-company-registration.whatIs: A Section 8 Company is a company formed for charitable or non-profit purposes. Any profit it makes must be used for its goals, not shared among members. It enjoys high trust because it follows company-level rules and transparency. It can also get tax exemptions (like 12A and 80G), which let donors claim tax benefits — making it easier to raise donations.
benefits: High credibility and trust for your cause
Can receive donations and grants
Eligible for tax exemptions (12A and 80G)
Donors can claim tax benefits, encouraging giving
Separate legal identity with limited liability
Recognised structure for serious social work
who: NGOs and charitable organisations
Foundations for education, health or environment
Social enterprises and welfare groups
Art, science and culture promotion bodies
Anyone running a serious non-profit
docs: PAN and Aadhaar of all directors
A No Objection letter from the property owner
Details of the company's charitable objectives
process: We help define your charitable objectives clearly
We get Digital Signatures (DSC) and DINs for directors
We apply for a special licence from the government to operate as a non-profit
We reserve your company name and file incorporation
You receive your Certificate of Incorporation
We help you apply for 12A and 80G tax exemptions
The full process usually takes 15 to 25 working days
faqs: What is the difference between a trust, society and Section 8 Company?
All three can run non-profits, but a Section 8 Company has the highest credibility and follows company rules, which donors and grant-givers trust most.
What are 12A and 80G?
12A gives your organisation tax exemption on its income. 80G lets your donors claim tax benefits on their donations. Both make fundraising easier. We help you get them.
Can a Section 8 Company make profit?
It can earn income, but the money must be used for its charitable goals — it cannot be shared among members as profit.
How long does registration take?
Usually 15 to 25 working days, as it needs a special government licence.
Can I pay salaries in a Section 8 Company?
Yes, you can pay reasonable salaries to staff for their work. What you cannot do is distribute profits to members.

trust-registration.meta: Trust Registration in India — for charitable and family trusts. Benefits, documents, process and tax exemptions explained simply by Tax Alphonic.
trust-registration.intro: A trust is one of the oldest and simplest ways to do charitable work or manage family assets in India. You set aside money or property to be used for a specific purpose — like helping the poor, running a school, or caring for your family — and trustees make sure it is used the right way. It is straightforward to set up and well suited to charity and family wealth planning.
trust-registration.whatIs: A trust is a legal arrangement where one party (the trustee) holds and manages assets for the benefit of others or for a cause. It is created through a document called a trust deed. There are two main types: public trusts (for charity, open to the public) and private trusts (for specific people, like a family). Charitable trusts can also get 12A and 80G tax benefits.
benefits: Simple and time-tested way to do charity
Good for managing family wealth and succession
Charitable trusts can get tax exemptions (12A, 80G)
Clear rules through the trust deed
Lower compliance than a company
Builds trust with donors and beneficiaries
who: People starting a charitable organisation
Families planning wealth and succession
Religious and educational institutions
Anyone setting aside assets for a cause
Groups wanting a simple non-profit structure
docs: PAN and Aadhaar of the trustees and settlor
Proof of the trust's registered address
The trust deed (we draft this for you)
process: We understand your purpose and who the trustees will be
We draft a clear trust deed setting out the objectives and rules
The settlor and trustees sign the deed
We register the trust with the local registrar
We help charitable trusts apply for 12A and 80G
You receive your registered trust deed, usually in 10 to 20 working days
faqs: What is the difference between a public and private trust?
A public trust is for charity and benefits the general public. A private trust benefits specific people, like family members. We help you choose the right one.
Can a trust get tax benefits?
Yes, charitable trusts can apply for 12A (tax exemption on income) and 80G (tax benefit for donors). We help you get both.
Who are the settlor and trustees?
The settlor is the person who creates the trust and puts in the assets. The trustees are the people who manage those assets as per the trust deed.
Is a trust better than a Section 8 Company?
A trust is simpler and good for charity and family planning. A Section 8 Company has higher credibility for large-scale work and grants. We advise based on your goal.
How long does it take?
Usually 10 to 20 working days, depending on your state and the type of trust.

public-limited-company-registration.meta: Public Limited Company Registration in India — raise capital from the public. Benefits, documents, process and timeline explained simply by Tax Alphonic.
public-limited-company-registration.intro: A Public Limited Company is built for big businesses that want to raise money from the public, including through the stock market. It can have unlimited shareholders and is seen as the most credible and large-scale business structure. If your vision is a large company that may one day list on a stock exchange, this is the structure for you.
public-limited-company-registration.whatIs: A Public Limited Company is a company that can offer its shares to the public and have unlimited shareholders. It needs at least three directors and seven shareholders to start. It follows stricter rules and more transparency than a private company, because it can take money from the public. This transparency is exactly what gives it high trust and credibility.
benefits: Can raise money from the public and investors
Can list on a stock exchange in the future
Unlimited number of shareholders allowed
Highest level of credibility and scale
Shares can be freely transferred
Strong structure for large businesses
who: Large businesses planning to scale big
Companies that may list on the stock market
Businesses wanting to raise large public capital
Established firms expanding operations
Founders with a large-scale vision
docs: PAN and Aadhaar of all directors (minimum 3)
Address proof of directors and shareholders
A No Objection letter from the property owner
process: We get Digital Signatures (DSC) and DINs for all directors
We reserve your company name
We prepare the detailed incorporation documents and company rules
We file everything with the government
The government reviews and approves
You receive your Certificate of Incorporation, PAN and TAN
The process usually takes 12 to 20 working days
faqs: How many people do I need for a Public Limited Company?
At least 3 directors and 7 shareholders to start. There is no maximum limit on shareholders.
Can a Public Limited Company list on the stock market?
Yes, that is one of its biggest advantages — it can offer shares to the public and list on a stock exchange after meeting the requirements.
How is it different from a Private Limited Company?
A public company can raise money from the public and have unlimited shareholders, but it follows stricter rules. A private company is smaller and more closely held.
Is the compliance heavy?
Yes, public companies have more rules and transparency requirements because they handle public money. We help you stay fully compliant.
How long does it take to register?
Usually 12 to 20 working days, given the additional documentation.

producer-company-registration.meta: Producer Company Registration in India — for farmers and producers. Benefits, documents, process and timeline explained simply by Tax Alphonic.
producer-company-registration.intro: A Producer Company is specially designed for farmers, growers and producers who want to come together and do business as one strong group. By joining hands, small producers get better prices, shared resources and a stronger market position. It is a powerful way for the people who actually produce — farmers, dairy producers, weavers — to take control and earn more.
producer-company-registration.whatIs: A Producer Company is a company formed by primary producers — like farmers, dairy farmers, fishermen or artisans. It combines the benefits of a cooperative with the structure of a company. The members are the producers themselves, and the company helps them with production, harvesting, marketing, selling and more. It needs at least 10 producers or 2 producer institutions to form.
benefits: Small producers gain strength by joining together
Better prices and bargaining power in the market
Shared resources, equipment and storage
Limited liability protection for members
Profits and benefits go back to the producers
Access to government schemes and support
who: Groups of farmers and growers
Dairy, poultry and fishery producers
Weavers, artisans and craftspeople
Agricultural producer groups
Any group of primary producers wanting to scale together
docs: PAN and Aadhaar of all members (minimum 10 producers)

faqs: Who can form a Producer Company?
At least 10 individual producers, or 2 producer institutions, or a combination. The members must be primary producers like farmers or artisans.
How is it different from a normal company?
A Producer Company is owned by producers themselves and exists to benefit them. Profits and gains flow back to the members, not outside investors.
What activities can it do?
Production, harvesting, procurement, grading, pooling, marketing, selling, and even providing equipment and education to members.
Do members get limited liability?
Yes, members' personal assets are protected, just like in a regular company.
How long does registration take?
Usually 15 to 25 working days.

indian-subsidiary-registration.meta: Indian Subsidiary Registration for foreign companies. Set up your company in India easily. Benefits, documents and process explained simply by Tax Alphonic.
indian-subsidiary-registration.intro: If you are a foreign company or an overseas business wanting to enter the huge Indian market, setting up an Indian Subsidiary is the most common and trusted way. It lets your foreign parent company own and run a company in India, fully and legally. India is one of the world's fastest-growing markets, and a subsidiary gives you a strong, official base here.
indian-subsidiary-registration.whatIs: An Indian Subsidiary is a company registered in India that is owned (fully or majority) by a foreign parent company. It is usually set up as a Private Limited Company. It is a separate legal entity under Indian law, so it can do business, hire staff, sign contracts and earn revenue in India, while being controlled by the foreign parent. It must follow Indian company law and FDI (foreign investment) rules.
benefits: A legal, official base to do business in India
The foreign parent can own up to 100% in most sectors
Access to India's large and growing market
Limited liability for the parent company
Can hire local staff and sign Indian contracts
Builds trust with Indian customers and partners
who: Foreign companies entering the Indian market
Overseas startups expanding to India
Global businesses setting up an India office
Foreign investors wanting an Indian presence
NRIs starting a company in India
docs: Documents of the foreign parent company (notarised/apostilled)
Passport and address proof of foreign directors
Proof of Indian registered office address
A No Objection letter from the property owner
At least one Indian resident director's documents
process: We advise on the right structure and check FDI rules for your sector
We get Digital Signatures (DSC) and DINs for directors
We reserve your company name
We prepare incorporation documents, including notarised foreign documents
We file with the government and handle FDI compliance
You receive your Certificate of Incorporation, PAN and TAN
The process usually takes 15 to 25 working days
faqs: Can a foreign company own 100% of an Indian subsidiary?
In most sectors, yes — 100% foreign ownership is allowed under the automatic route. Some sectors have limits. We check the rules for your specific business.
Do I need an Indian director?
Yes, an Indian subsidiary must have at least one director who is a resident of India. We can guide you on this requirement.
What is FDI compliance?
FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) rules govern how foreign money comes into India. After investment, certain filings must be made with the RBI. We handle this for you.
How long does it take?
Usually 15 to 25 working days, as foreign documents need notarisation and apostille.
What structure is best for a subsidiary?
Most foreign companies set up their Indian subsidiary as a Private Limited Company, as it is flexible and widely accepted.

businessComplianceFaqs: What is Business Compliance Management?

It is an annual managed service where Tax Alphonic acts as your outsourced compliance department — handling registrations, licences, renewals, statutory filings, documentation and government notices for the whole year under one plan.
Why should I outsource compliance instead of doing it in-house?

An in-house team covering CA, CS, labour and licensing work is expensive and hard to retain. Outsourcing gives you the same expertise at a predictable annual cost, with no single-person dependency and no missed deadlines.
How is the annual fee decided?

It depends on your entity type, number of registrations and licences, states of operation, employee count and industry. We run a free compliance audit first, then quote a fixed annual plan with no hidden charges.
Which registrations are mandatory for my business?
It varies by structure, turnover, industry and state. Use our industry selector or book a free consultation and we will give you an exact mandatory-versus-optional checklist for your business.
What happens if a compliance deadline is missed?
Missed filings usually attract penalties, interest and in some cases licence suspension or director disqualification. Our calendar, tracking and reminders exist specifically to prevent this.
Can you manage compliance for multiple branches and states?
Yes. Multi-state and multi-branch compliance is handled under a single plan, with state-specific labour, licensing and tax requirements mapped separately.
Do you handle government notices and inspections?
Yes. We track every notice, draft and file the reply, and support you through departmental inspections and audits until the matter is closed.
Will I get a dedicated person to talk to?
Yes — Professional plans and above include a dedicated compliance manager as your single point of contact, backed by our CA, CS, legal and labour specialists.
Which industries do you cover?
We support a wide range of sectors including manufacturing, healthcare, food, construction, security and manpower, IT, education, logistics, retail, e-commerce, real estate and financial services.
How do we get started?
Book a free consultation or request a compliance audit. We review your current status, share a gap report and a fixed annual plan, and take over from there.
